cls: Erythroid maturation agent (TGF-beta ligand trap, Reblozyl)
pharm: Recombinant fusion protein trapping TGF-beta superfamily ligands (GDF11, activin B); restores late-stage erythropoiesis and reduces transfusion burden in MDS and beta-thalassaemia
quick: 1-1.75 mg/kg SC every 3 weeks (MDS); beta-thalassaemia per labeling titration
Not applicable - subcutaneous injection in clinic
May cause fetal harm; verify status; effective contraception during and for 3 months after last dose
No human milk data; avoid breastfeeding during treatment
No adjustment in mild-moderate impairment; monitor blood pressure and renal function
No formal adjustment; monitor (limited severe-impairment data)
summary: Luspatercept (Reblozyl) is a first-in-class erythroid maturation agent for anaemia of lower-risk myelodysplastic syndromes (including ESA-naive and RS-positive disease) and transfusion-dependent beta-thalassaemia. By trapping TGF-beta ligands it restores late-stage red-cell maturation rather than stimulating early progenitors like ESAs. Key risks are thromboembolism (higher with splenectomy, prior clots or HRT), hypertension, headache, bone pain and embryo-fetal toxicity.
indications: Anaemia of very-low to intermediate-risk myelodysplastic syndromes requiring red-cell transfusions
Anaemia of beta-thalassaemia requiring regular red-cell transfusions

dosage.d: Start 1 mg/kg every 3 weeks; escalate to 1.33 then 1.75 mg/kg if transfusion burden persists (no response after 2 doses at a level)
dosage.t: SC into upper arm, thigh or abdomen in clinic; review Hb before each dose - hold if pre-dose Hb high per labeling
dosage.n: Dose-hold/reduce for grade 3+ hypertension or lack of response

dosage.d: Start 1 mg/kg every 3 weeks; escalate to 1.25 mg/kg if transfusion burden persists
dosage.t: Same SC procedure; monitor iron chelation needs as transfusions fall

admin: Subcutaneous injection by a healthcare professional every 3 weeks; rotate sites
Review pre-dose haemoglobin and blood pressure before each injection
Continue iron chelation as directed - needs usually fall as transfusions decrease
Thromboprophylaxis per risk (splenectomy, prior thrombosis, hormonal therapy raise risk)
moa: Luspatercept is an activin-receptor-IIB-Fc fusion protein that binds TGF-beta superfamily ligands (notably GDF11 and activin B), dampening Smad2/3 signalling that blocks late-stage erythroid maturation. Distinct from erythropoiesis-stimulating agents, it acts on late precursors, improving red-cell quality and quantity.

relative: Prior thromboembolism, splenectomy or hormonal therapy (higher clot risk)

preg: No adequate human data. Based on mechanism, fetal harm is expected. Verify pregnancy status before starting; advise effective contraception during treatment and for the specified period after the last dose. Use in pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential fetal risk. Advise effective contraception during treatment and for at least 3 months after the final dose.
lact: No data on presence in human milk. Avoid breastfeeding during treatment and advise on alternative feeding.
renal: No dose adjustment in mild-moderate renal impairment; monitor blood pressure and renal function. Limited data in severe impairment.
hepatic: No formal dose adjustment in hepatic impairment; monitor closely (limited data in severe impairment).

major: Hormonal contraception/HRT (may add to thrombosis risk - assess)
moderate: Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (not co-administered; sequential per protocol)
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory test interference; monitor disease-specific markers.

serious: Thromboembolic events (DVT, pulmonary embolism, stroke, portal-vein thrombosis)
emergency: Leg swelling/pain, sudden breathlessness or chest pain (possible clot) - seek emergency care
Sudden weakness, speech or vision change (possible stroke) - seek emergency care
Severely high blood pressure with headache/chest pain - seek emergency care

monitoring: Pre-dose haemoglobin and transfusion record every cycle
Thrombosis risk review (splenectomy, prior clot, hormones)
counsel: Attend every-3-week injection visits; transfusion needs usually fall gradually, not at once
Report leg swelling/pain, breathlessness, chest pain or sudden weakness at once (clot signs)
Check blood pressure as instructed; report severe headache
Keep taking iron chelation until the team changes it; use contraception during and for 3 months after
pk: Haemoglobin rise over weeks; transfusion reduction assessed over 12-24 weeks
Refrigerate 2-8 C; do not freeze; use reconstituted solution promptly per labeling
pearls: Acts on late-stage erythropoiesis (unlike ESAs) - hence activity in ring-sideroblast/SF3B1 MDS
Transfusion-burden response, not a single Hb number, judges continuation and escalation
Thrombosis risk concentrates with splenectomy/prior clots - risk-stratify before starting
missed: Give the missed dose as soon as possible and maintain the every-3-week interval from the actual dose date; do not double.
overdose: No specific antidote. Overdose may exaggerate hypertension, headache and thrombotic risk. Withhold drug, monitor blood pressure and clot signs, and give supportive care. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
